result.final_text:
## What this letter says
This letter gives your test results. You had a camera test of your stomach (gastroscopy). Small samples were taken (biopsies). This was on 8 September 2026.

- The samples show no cancer (no evidence of malignancy).
- There is no sign of Helicobacter pylori infection.
- The samples did show changes called intestinal metaplasia. This is a change in the lining of your stomach. It is not cancer.
- In a small number of people, it can develop further over many years. So the doctors watch it.

## What you need to do
1. Continue omeprazole 20 milligrams once daily.
2. Stop taking ibuprofen and other anti-inflammatory painkillers. The letter says they can irritate the stomach.
3. You can use paracetamol instead.
4. You do not need to do anything now about the repeat gastroscopy. The hospital will send you an appointment.

## Dates and medicines
- 8 September 2026: your gastroscopy and biopsies.
- Around September 2029: repeat gastroscopy, in 3 years. The hospital will send you an appointment.
- Omeprazole: 20 milligrams, once daily. Continue.
- Ibuprofen and the other painkillers: stop.
- Paracetamol: you can use it instead.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- What does this stomach change mean for me?
- Why do I need a repeat gastroscopy?
- Can I use paracetamol instead of ibuprofen?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
